module.title: Oven spring and crust
module.summary: Use heat, steam and timing to set the loaf you shaped.
objectives: Explain oven spring and crust colour as consequences of heat and steam.

scenarios.title: Fix a pale, well-risen loaf
scenarios.context: A fictional home baker reports tall loaves with soft, pale crusts from a covered pot. No oven or real bakery is involved.
scenarios.task: Propose one change to the bake and explain the mechanism you expect it to change.
requirements: State the decision and the evidence behind it.
Name one alternative and how you would compare the results.
scenarios.model: Uncover the pot earlier and finish the bake dry. The height shows the steam phase worked; the pale crust shows the surface stayed moist too long to brown. Compare two bakes that differ only in when the lid comes off.
scenarios.reasoning: A strong response ties each choice to evidence the baker can observe, keeps an alternative open and says what result would change the plan.

rubric.weak: States a rule or a time with no evidence.
rubric.partial: Names relevant evidence but leaves the decision vague.
rubric.strong: Connects the decision to observable evidence and names what would change it.

disclosures.question: What does the fictional baker care about most?
disclosures.response: A loaf they can explain and repeat. There is no single correct style.

concepts.definition: Oven spring is the rapid rise in the first minutes of baking, as trapped gas expands and water turns to steam. A crust that sets too early limits it.
